strategy.executive_summary: Saffron Table Group runs five full-service restaurants in Amsterdam with about 120 staff and a six-person office team covering HR, finance, and marketing. Your teams already use digital tools for reservations, point of sale, rota planning, supplier ordering, accounting, and reviews, but most follow-up, reporting, and admin work is still manual. The best first wins are in reservations, event quotes, supplier invoices, and rota admin, where small agents can save your team time without changing how the restaurants run. We suggest starting with a few focused agents and keeping humans in control of guest-facing and money decisions. Total realistic savings from the plan below are about 92 staff hours per week across 120 employees.

maturity.label: Early stage
maturity.note: You have core systems in place but no AI agents in daily use. Most guest replies, quotes, roster changes, invoice entry, and reporting are handled by hand, so gains depend on clean data and simple approvals.

opportunities.title: Reservation emails and phone requests handled faster
opportunities.department: Front of House and Restaurant Operations
opportunities.description: An agent reads booking emails and web forms, checks table availability in your reservation system, and drafts replies with options or waitlist offers. It sends routine confirmations and flags special requests, large parties, and allergy notes to the right manager.
before: Guest emails or calls the restaurant.
Host checks the reservation system table by table.
Host replies with available times or adds to waitlist.
Manager handles special requests if time allows.
No-shows and waitlist are updated later.
after: Agent reads the booking request and checks availability.
Agent drafts a reply with two or three suitable times.
Human: Host approves and sends, or edits if needed.
Agent updates the reservation system and waitlist.
Agent flags large parties and allergy notes to the manager.

opportunities.title: Event quotes prepared in under an hour
opportunities.description: An agent turns event inquiry emails into a first draft quote using your menu, minimum spend, and staffing rules. It checks kitchen availability, adds allergen notes, and follows up on quotes that have not been answered.
before: Inquiry arrives by email or phone.
Coordinator asks kitchen for date availability.
Coordinator builds quote from old documents.
Client waits for a reply.
Follow-up happens only if someone remembers.
after: Agent reads the inquiry and extracts date, headcount, and budget.
Agent checks event calendar and kitchen capacity.
Agent drafts quote with menu options and allergen notes.
Human: Events Coordinator reviews and sends.
Agent schedules follow-up reminders and logs the reply.

opportunities.title: Supplier invoices entered and matched
opportunities.description: An agent reads supplier invoices from email or PDF, codes them to the right restaurant and supplier, and checks them against orders in your stock or accounting system. It prepares the payment run list and flags price changes or missing delivery notes.
before: Invoices arrive by email and post.
Assistant opens each invoice and types details into accounting.
Assistant matches invoice to supplier order manually.
Finance Manager checks exceptions.
Payment run is prepared from a spreadsheet.
after: Agent collects invoices from email and shared folder.
Agent extracts supplier, amount, VAT, and invoice number.
Agent matches to purchase orders and flags differences.
Human: Accounts Assistant checks flagged items and approves.
Agent prepares payment run list for Finance Manager.

opportunities.title: Rota gaps filled and holiday requests processed
opportunities.description: An agent tracks holiday requests, checks rota rules, and drafts approval replies. When a shift gap appears, it messages available staff by role and updates the rota once a manager approves.
before: Staff send holiday requests by email or app.
HR Assistant checks rota and contract rules.
Manager approves or rejects by email.
Shift gaps are posted in staff group chats.
Rota is updated manually.
after: Agent reads holiday requests and checks rota rules.
Agent drafts approval or rejection for HR.
Human: HR or Manager approves.
Agent messages available staff when a gap appears.
Agent updates rota after manager confirms.

opportunities.title: Guest reviews answered within one day
opportunities.description: An agent drafts replies to Google and TripAdvisor reviews in your brand voice and routes serious complaints to the right restaurant manager. It tracks common themes such as waiting times, noise, or menu requests and sends a weekly summary.
before: Reviews sit unanswered for days.
Coordinator reads each review and writes a reply.
Serious complaints are forwarded by email.
Themes are noticed only anecdotally.
Weekly report is made by hand.
after: Agent collects new reviews each morning.
Agent drafts a reply and a suggested action.
Human: Coordinator or Manager approves and posts.
Agent routes serious complaints to the right manager.
Agent sends a weekly themes summary.

opportunities.title: Prep lists and supplier orders drafted overnight
opportunities.description: An agent reviews upcoming bookings, current stock, and menu plans to draft prep lists and supplier orders. It flags low stock and waste risks, then sends the draft to the Head Chef for approval.
before: Head Chef checks bookings and stock.
Sous Chef writes prep lists by hand.
Orders are placed by phone or supplier portal.
Stock gaps are found during service.
Waste is reviewed after the week.
after: Agent reads bookings, stock, and menu plan.
Agent drafts prep list by section and shift.
Agent drafts supplier order with quantities.
Human: Head Chef reviews and approves.
Agent sends order and saves prep list for kitchen.

opportunities.title: Allergen answers ready for waitstaff
opportunities.description: An agent keeps a searchable allergen and menu guide updated from kitchen sheets and supplier labels. Waitstaff can ask it plain questions and get an answer with the source and date.
before: Waitstaff ask kitchen about allergens during service.
Kitchen checks paper sheets or packets.
Head Chef updates allergen records by hand.
Answers vary between shifts.
New menu items are added slowly.
after: Agent reads kitchen allergen sheets and supplier labels.
Agent builds a searchable guide by dish.
Human: Head Chef checks and approves new entries.
Waitstaff ask the agent plain questions during prep.
Agent shows the source and last update date.

opportunities.title: Daily sales and covers report ready by 9am
opportunities.department: Front of House and Restaurant Operations
opportunities.description: An agent pulls sales, covers, and average spend from the POS and sends a short morning digest for each restaurant. It highlights unusual drops, busy periods, and staff cost against sales.
before: Managers log into POS for each site.
They export sales and covers to spreadsheets.
Finance checks numbers later in the week.
Issues are spotted late.
Reports are shared in separate emails.
after: Agent pulls previous day sales and covers from POS.
Agent compares to last week and target.
Agent writes a short digest per restaurant.
Human: Restaurant Manager reviews and acts.
Agent sends weekly summary to Finance.

opportunities.title: New hire onboarding paperwork chased automatically
opportunities.description: An agent sends new hires the right forms, tracks what is missing, and reminds managers about expiring documents. It keeps a simple dashboard of who is ready to work and what is still outstanding.
before: HR sends forms manually.
New hire returns some documents by email.
HR chases missing items one by one.
Managers are told late about missing papers.
Compliance dates are tracked in a spreadsheet.
after: Agent sends welcome pack and forms from templates.
Agent tracks returned documents and missing items.
Agent sends reminders to new hire and manager.
Human: HR checks exceptions and approves.
Agent updates compliance dashboard and expiry alerts.

roadmap.title: Start with reservation and review agents
items: Pick one restaurant as the pilot site.
Connect the reservation system, shared inbox, and review accounts.
Set rules for when a human must approve guest replies.
Train hosts and managers on the approval step.
Measure time saved and reply speed each week.

roadmap.title: Add finance and events agents
items: Launch supplier invoice entry and matching for one accounting system.
Launch event quote drafts with the Events Coordinator.
Add holiday request and rota gap support for HR and managers.
Send weekly review themes to Marketing and Restaurant Managers.
Review accuracy and adjust approval rules.

roadmap.title: Expand to kitchen and HR, then improve
items: Add prep list and supplier order drafts for the kitchen.
Add the allergen and menu guide for waitstaff.
Add onboarding and compliance chase for HR.
Run a monthly check on hours saved, errors, and staff feedback.
Decide which agents to keep, change, or stop.

risks.risk: The agent sends an incorrect reply to a guest.
risks.mitigation: Keep human approval for all guest-facing messages and set clear escalation rules for complaints and allergies.

risks.risk: Staff do not use the agents because they add extra steps.
risks.mitigation: Start with one team, keep the approval step simple, and ask managers to name a champion for each agent.

risks.risk: Data privacy or GDPR issues with guest, staff, or supplier data.
risks.mitigation: Keep data inside approved systems, limit access by role, and review supplier terms before connecting any tool.

risks.risk: Integration problems with POS, reservation, rota, or accounting systems.
risks.mitigation: Connect one system at a time, keep a manual fallback, and test with real data before going live.

risks.risk: The team relies on the agent and misses exceptions.
risks.mitigation: Set review thresholds, run weekly accuracy checks, and keep a named person responsible for each agent.

kpis: Staff hours saved per week by agent, target 90 by month 6.

Event quote turnaround, target under 24 hours.

Rota gaps filled without manager overtime, target 80 percent within 4 hours.
